# War Scroll Column 8 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 1QM (Cave 1), Col. 8 | **Condition:** fragmentary (damage at bottom)

---

**1** The horsemen of the cavalry shall be deployed in two wings, flanking the body of the formation to the right and to the left.

**2** One wing shall set out to press against the flank of the enemy, and the other wing to press against their rear, so as to surround them.

**3** The two wings of the cavalry shall go forth together to crush the spirit of the enemy and to scatter them before the Sons of Light.

**4** The horses of battle shall be stallions, trained for war, accustomed to the sound of tumult and to the sight of slaughter.

**5** They shall not shy away from any sound nor be terrified by any sight; rather, they shall be stout of heart and swift of foot.

**6** Their age shall be from four years to eight years, and they shall be chosen from open lands where the pasture is good.

**7** They shall not be driven to exhaustion before battle, for they must be fresh and ready on the day of engagement.

**8** Those who ride upon them — the riders of the cavalry — shall be men from thirty to forty-five years of age, mighty men of war.

**9** Their armor shall consist of a breastplate of bronze upon their chests, greaves of bronze upon their legs, and a helmet of bronze upon their heads.

**10** A shield shall be in their left hand, and in their right hand a battle lance six cubits in length, and a sword girded upon their thigh.

**11** They shall ride into the spaces between the battle lines but shall not enter the ranks of the infantry, lest they trample them.

**12** When the cavalry charge, they shall ride between the formations to strike down the enemy, and the trumpeters shall blow a signal for their advance.

**13** The horsemen shall pursue those who flee and shall cut them down until they are consumed, and none shall escape.

**14** In the engagement of battle, the cavalry shall wheel to the right and to the left [...] the flanks of the enemy.

**15** [...] and they shall press upon them [...] and the slain shall fall [...] before the Sons of Light.

**16** [...] the horsemen [...] the battle [...] the formation [...]

**17** [...] on the day of [...] God [...] victory [...]

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 8 is well preserved through line 13, with progressive damage from line 14 onward. The cavalry tactics described (two-wing flanking, pursuit of fleeing enemy) reflect Hellenistic-era military conventions. Horse age requirements (4-8 years) and the detailed armor catalogue (lines 9-10) demonstrate the scroll's concern with practical military detail alongside its eschatological vision.*
